item.title: 🔴 Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP Require Immediate Patching
item.description:
Why this matters: Remote-code-execution risk — assess exposure and patch or mitigate quickly.

CISA strongly urges organizations to immediately patch the recently disclosed critical vulnerabilities in PHP, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. These vulnerabilities, known as “php2shell,” allow for unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP and affect all PHP installations serving web requests. Organizations should immediately update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35 to fix these vulnerabilities. While CISA has not observed exploitation of these vulnerabilities as of the time of publication, they pose a risk to organizations if left unpatched. 

CISA urges organizations to take the following actions:

  • Identify and inventory systems running any version of PHP across your organization. 
    • PHP is often a component of other software and prevalence may not be directly observable.
  • Apply the patch immediately, prioritizing internet-facing systems.
  • Organizations that cannot update immediately, or that continue to use PHP 8.1 or earlier unsupported versions, should take PHP-based systems offline until they can be patched or updated.
  • A web application firewall may provide some protection until systems are updated or patched.
  • Review the official PHP security advisory for guidance on patching.

    • Source: CISA Alerts  |  Severity: Critical  |  Age: 12h

item.title: 🔴 PHP core RCE vulnerability patches (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619)
item.description:
Why this matters: Remote-code-execution risk — assess exposure and patch or mitigate quickly.

CVSSv3 Score: 9.8

CVE-2026-109618PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

Revised on 2026-10-21 00:00:00



Source: Fortinet PSIRT  |  Severity: Critical  |  Age: 17h

item.title: 🔴 #StopRansomware: SafePay Ransomware
item.description:
Why this matters: Elevated ransomware risk — validate backups, endpoint protection, and recovery readiness.

Advisory at a Glance

Title #StopRansomware: SafePay Ransomware
Original Publication  October 20, 2026
Executive Summary

This advisory details recent activity by the SafePay ransomware group. SafePay actors have been highly active since August 2024, targeting businesses and critical infrastructure across North America, South America, Europe, and Australia. SafePay actors typically gain access to networks by stealing or guessing passwords, exploiting vulnerabilities in security systems, and using phishing tactics. 

Once inside the network, SafePay actors establish control by creating new accounts or taking over existing ones. They then use legitimate system tools to move through the network, identify valuable files, and disable security protections to avoid detection. Next, they encrypt the victim’s files, making them inaccessible, and leave a ransom note demanding payment in cryptocurrency. This advisory urges organizations to follow recommended security measures to reduce the risk and impact of SafePay ransomware attacks.

item.title: 🔴 CISA Urges Patching Critical Vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and watch for suspicious sign-ins.

CISA is aware of critical authentication bypass vulnerability CVE-2026-102764, affecting BeyondTrust Remote Support (formerly Bomgar) versions 26.2.3 and earlier. Patches are available for supported versions (24.3.1 and later); organizations using older versions must upgrade first. Cyber threat actors are actively exploiting the vulnerability to gain initial access, then establishing persistence, escalating privileges, and moving laterally. CISA added CVE-2026-102764 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on Oct. 16, 2026. 

CISA urges organizations with affected self-hosted Remote Support appliances to immediately take the following actions: 

  1. Apply the BT26-05-RS patch, as outlined in BeyondTrust’s Security Advisory BT26-05. Organizations on a self-hosted Remote Support version older than 24.3.1 will need to upgrade to a newer version to apply the patch. Organizations using BeyondTrust-hosted (SaaS) Remote Support deployments have already been patched. Review BeyondTrust’s blog ARMORY CASTLE and BT26-05: What Security Teams Need to Know for detailed information on the vulnerability and recommended response…

    Source: CISA Alerts  |  Severity: Critical  |  Age: 5d
